{{Current events|year=2021|month=01|day=12|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eight people die in an apartment building fire in [[Yekaterinburg]], [[Russia]]. Investigators say that the preliminary cause of death is [[carbon monoxide poisoning]]. [https://www.znak.com/2021-01-12/zhenchina_pisavshaya_v_twitter_o_pozhare_v_ekaterinburge_ne_mogla_dozvonitsya_v_mchs (Znak)]
*A [[barge]] travelling from [[Kisangani]] to the town of [[Basoko]] in [[Tshopo]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], sinks in the [[Congo River]]. Local authorities report that at least six people were killed and 19 others are missing. [https://www.brecorder.com/news/40050332/six-dead-19-missing-in-congo-river-barge-sinking (AFP via ''Business Recorder'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario]]
*****[[Premier of Ontario|Premier]] [[Doug Ford]] announces a second state of emergency and [[stay-at-home order|stay-at-home]] order for [[Ontario]] as the number of cases continues to increase. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7571036/ontario-new-restrictions-lockdown-coronavirus/ (Global News)]
****[[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian Prime Minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] announces that [[Canada|the country]] will double its order of the [[Pfizer]]-[[BioNTech]] [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from 20 million to 40 million doses. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-canada-pfizer/canada-orders-20-million-more-doses-of-pfizer-biontech-covid-19-vaccine-pm-idUSKBN29H2AT (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
*****[[Maryland]] reports their first two cases of a new variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in a married couple from [[Anne Arundel County, Maryland|Anne Arundel County]], one of whom had travelled to the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://baltimore.cbslocal.com/2021/01/12/uk-covid-19-variant-detected-in-maryland/ (WJZ-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
*****The outgoing [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] announces that they will make changes to their [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] distributions in an effort to speed up the rollout. [https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/01/12/956017635/trump-administration-to-change-covid-19-vaccination-guidance-to-speed-up-rollout (NPR)]
****The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] announces that they will expand their order to require travelers from the [[United Kingdom]] to test negative for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/health-news/articles/2021-01-12/cdc-expands-negative-coronavirus-testing-requirements-for-international-air-travelers (U.S. News & World Report)]
****The [[United States]] reports a record 4,197 new deaths in the past 24 hours. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/12/health/us-coronavirus-tuesday/index.html (CNN)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[China|Chinese]] authorities place 4.9 million people in [[Langfang]] under [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for the next seven days and also subject them to mass [[COVID-19 testing|testing]] in an attempt to reduce the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/another-chinese-city-goes-into-lockdown-amid-new-covid-19-threat/46278842 (Swiss Info)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 302 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 24,645. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5330800/update-corona-ri-12-januari-rekor-302-kematian-dan-10-ribu-kasus-baru (detikHealth)]
****The [[Government of Indonesia|government]] receives 15 million doses of the half-finished [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by [[Sinovac Biotech]] for final production and distribution by [[Bio Farma]]. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/indonesia-receives-15-million-doses-of-halffinished-sinovac-vaccine (Jakarta Globe)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]]n [[Yang di-Pertuan Agong]] [[Abdullah of Pahang]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in the country until August 1 amid an increase in COVID-19 cases, suspending [[Parliament of Malaysia|parliament]] for the first time since 1969 for the remainder of the [[pandemic]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-12/malaysia-declares-state-of-emergency-as-pandemic-worsens (Bloomberg)]
****Malaysia reports a record 3,309 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours ahead of the return of [[Malaysian movement control order|movement control orders]] in parts of the country, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 141,553. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-posts-record-daily-rise-in-covid-19-cases-ahead-of-fresh-movement-curbs (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] plans to extend the ongoing state of emergency to locations outside of the [[Greater Tokyo Area]]. [https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1102923/state-of-emergency-osaka-kyoto-hyogo (Insidethegames)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
****[[Kyrgyzstan]] receives documents for [[Pfizer]]'s [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://en.trend.az/casia/kyrgyzstan/3363447.html (Trend)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Bavaria]]n [[List of Ministers-President of Bavaria|Ministers-President]] [[Markus Söder]] announces that starting from next Monday, people will be required to wear [[FFP standards|FFP2]] masks while travelling on public transport and when in retail shops in order to improve safety on these areas. [https://www.thelocal.de/20210112/bavaria-orders-compulsory-ffp2-masks-on-public-transport-and-in-shops (''The Local Germany'')]
****[[Baden-Württemberg]] reports [[Germany]]'s first case of [[501.V2 variant|new variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in a family that travelled from [[South Africa]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/south-african-covid-variant-found-in-germany/a-56205752 (DW)]  
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] extends its nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until February 9 despite the number of new cases falling. [https://www.government.nl/latest/news/2021/01/12/netherlands-to-remain-in-lockdown-until-at-least-9-february-inclusive (Government of the Netherlands)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 155 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 8,080. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/316_DGS_boletim_20210112.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Spain]] receives their first shipment of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna vaccine]]. [https://www.aninews.in/news/world/europe/spain-receives-first-batch-of-moderna-covid-19-vaccine20210112184853 (ANI)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
****[[Swissmedic]] grants authorization for use of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna vaccine]] in [[Switzerland]], making it the second [[COVID-19 vaccine]] to be approved in the country. [https://www.swissmedic.ch/swissmedic/en/home/news/coronavirus-covid-19/zulassung-covid-19-impfstoff-moderna.html (Swissmedic)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia]]
***Former [[President of Bolivia|President]] [[Evo Morales]] tested positive for COVID-19. [https://g1.globo.com/mundo/noticia/2021/01/13/ex-presidente-da-bolivia-evo-morales-e-diagnosticado-com-coronavirus.ghtml (G1)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Egypt–Qatar relations]], [[Qatar diplomatic crisis]]
**[[Egypt]] reopens its airspace to [[Qatar]]i aircraft, and will allow the resumption of direct flights between the countries, which have been suspended since 2017. [https://www.reuters.com/article/gulf-qatar-egypt-int/egypt-reopens-airspace-to-qatar-sources-state-media-say-idUSKBN29H161 (Reuters)]
*[[Moldova–Ukraine relations]]
**[[President of Moldova|Moldovan President]] [[Maia Sandu]] arrives in [[Ukraine]] for her first foreign visit as president. Both countries said that they are willing to join the [[Three Seas Initiative]] and [[European Union]]. [https://uawire.org/moldovan-president-arrives-in-ukraine-on-her-first-foreign-visit (UAWire.org)] [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-economy/3169575-ukraine-moldova-willing-to-join-three-seas-initiative.html (Ukrinform)] [https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/europe/ukraine-and-moldova-presidents-support-joining-european-union.html (Republic TV)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[2021 efforts to remove Donald Trump from office]]
***[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] warns that successfully impeaching him from office for his conduct regarding the riot at the [[United States Capitol Building]] would represent a "tremendous danger" to the nation. Trump refused to clarify his statement any further, instead stating that his comments vis-à-vis inciting the incident were "totally appropriate". [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/12/trump-warns-impeachment-is-a-danger-to-us-in-first-public-comments-since-riot.html (CNBC)]
***[[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] tells [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]] that he won't invoke the [[Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution|25th amendment]]. [https://www.chicagotribune.com/election-2020/ct-trump-capitol-riot-20210112-ltxwk656xreaxftpvqolxgvska-story.html (''Chicago Tribune'')]  
*[[2021 Ugandan general election]]
**Ahead of Thursday's election, [[Uganda]]n opposition [[President of Uganda|presidential]] candidate [[Bobi Wine]] says that [[Uganda People's Defence Force|soldiers]] raided his home and arrested his security guards without providing any explanation. Wine has previously been accused by incumbent [[Yoweri Museveni]] of being "an agent of foreign interests". [https://www.dw.com/en/uganda-presidential-candidate-bobi-wine-says-army-raided-his-home-arrested-staff/a-56199731 (DW)]
**In retaliation against [[Facebook]] for blocking pro-government accounts, the government of Uganda blocks all social media, including [[Facebook]] and [[WhatsApp]] until further notice. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-uganda-election-social-media/uganda-orders-all-social-media-to-be-blocked-letter-idUSKBN29H1E7?il=0 (Reuters)]
*Aftermath of the [[poisoning of Alexei Navalny]]
**Authorities in [[Russia]] ask a judge to jail opposition politician and anti-corruption activist [[Alexei Navalny]] for allegedly breaking a suspended sentence dating back to 2014 and for evading the supervision of Russia's criminal inspection authority. Navalny had previously been asked to return to Russia to report himself to the federal authorities but continues to remain in [[Germany]]. He has vowed to return to Russia ahead of the next parliamentary election. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-politics-navalny/russian-judge-is-asked-to-jail-kremlin-critic-alexei-navalny-in-absentia-idUSKBN29H1KG?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The [[Jordan]]ian [[State Security Court]] sentences a man [[Capital punishment in Jordan|to death]] for perpetrating a [[Stabbing as a terrorist tactic|stabbing attack]] on eight people in [[Jerash]] in November 2019. The court alleges that the man "had been in contact with one of the members of the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]", although the organization never [[List of terrorist incidents linked to ISIL|claimed responsibility]] formally. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/middle-east/20210112-jordanian-sentenced-to-death-for-2019-tourist-stabbings (AFP via RFI)]
*The [[Supreme Court of Sri Lanka]] sentences former member of [[Parliament of Sri Lanka|parliament]] [[Ranjan Ramanayake]], who is affiliated with the opposition [[United National Party]], to a four-year "rigorous imprisonment" over his remarks claiming that most [[Judiciary of Sri Lanka|judges]] in [[Sri Lanka|the country]] were "[[Corruption in Sri Lanka|corrupt]]". [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/south-asia/sri-lanka-jails-ex-minister-for-saying-judges-are-corrupt/articleshow/80237240.cms (AFP via ''The Times of India'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Presidential transition of Joe Biden]]
**[[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] acknowledges that the [[Presidency of Donald Trump|Trump presidency]] is coming to an end, and said that the administration is working with [[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]]'s transition team. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/533880-pence-promises-governors-smooth-transition-in-task-force-call (''The Hill'')]
**The [[Joint Chiefs of Staff]] condemn the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]], and acknowledge Biden's victory. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/12/top-military-leaders-condemn-sedition-and-insurrection-at-capitol-acknowledge-biden-win.html (CNBC)]
*[[Presidency of Donald Trump]]
**Donald Trump visits [[Alamo, Texas]], giving a speech at [[Mexico–United States barrier|the Wall]] separating the [[United States–Mexico border]]. [https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2021/01/12/trump-heads-to-south-texas-for-victory-lap-at-border-wall/ (''Dallas Morning News'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[2021 Formula One World Championship]]
**[[Formula One]] postpones the [[Australian Grand Prix|Australian]] and [[Chinese Grand Prix]] due to [[COVID-19]]-related restrictions. The Australian Grand Prix will take place in November instead of March, while the discussion over a new date for the Chinese Grand Prix is ongoing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/formula1/55625606 (BBC)]
